title: Introduce throughput-fingerprint prober and traffic-cohort gating policy
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add a lightweight throughput fingerprint prober and introduce a cohort-aware gating policy for canary rollouts; improves detection of throughput regressions in mixed-traffic environments and adds a graceful pause for cohorts that diverge significantly.
description:
Motivation: Canary detectors focused on latency fingerprints struggle to surface throughput regressions when traffic mixes multiple user cohorts with different request sizing and arrival patterns. This PR adds a near-real-time throughput fingerprint prober and a traffic-cohort gating policy that reduces false positives by conditioning alerts on cohort-aligned baselines. Changes include a new prober module that computes compact per-window throughput fingerprints, a cohorting service that assigns traffic using stable hashing and feature hints, and a gating controller that enforces cohort-aware thresholds during canary analysis. The description below outlines design, implementation, testing, and rollout plan.
Design: - Throughput fingerprint: multi-resolution histogram of inter-arrival deltas and per-request token counts computed with reservoir sampling; outputs are hashed and quantized into a small footprint vector (64 bytes) to allow efficient differential comparison across time windows.
- Cohorting: traffic is grouped by stable prefix-hash of routing key + optional meta-features (client_type, token_distribution_bucket). Cohorts are dynamic; a light-weight drift detector will retire cohorts inactive for >1h.
- Gate policy: when evaluating canaries, the detector computes per-cohort delta in throughput fingerprint distance (Jensen-Shannon on smoothed histograms). If any cohort crosses configured delta or experiences simultaneous throughput drop >X% and p99 tail shift, the rollout is paused and an automated investigation probe is triggered.
Implementation highlights: - perf_canary/prober/throughput_fingerprint.py: implements reservoir sampling, multi-res histograms, compact hash output, incremental delta update hooks.
- perf_canary/cohort/assigner.py: stable hashing + rules engine to attach request to cohort.
- perf_canary/gates/cohort_gate.py: gating logic, threshold tuning knobs, integration with existing canary orchestrator.
- integrations: telemetry -> metrics export via openmetrics; stored as compressed fingerprint series in the canary TTL store for 48h.
Compatibility and safety: - Fingerprint generation is opt-in for existing canaries (config flag canary.use_throughput_fingerprints). Default thresholds are conservative to avoid noisy pauses.
- Memory/CPU: prober uses bounded buffers and async IO; local CPU < 2% on production canaries in our internal trials.
Tests and validation: - Unit tests for sampling and fingerprint stability (perf_canary/tests/test_throughput_fingerprint.py).
- Golden regression tests comparing controlled synthetic workloads (burst, steady, bimodal) against baseline detectors.
- Canary lab: deployed to canary cluster with synthetic mixed cohorts for 72h. Observations: improved signal-to-noise for throughput regressions; minor tuning required for very sparse cohorts (handled by automatic cohort retirement).
Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag behind canary.use_throughput_fingerprints = off by default. 2) Stage to small subset of internal tenants (10%) for 1 week. 3) Increase to 50% with monitoring dashboards and alert set to notify SRE on first automated pause. 4) Full release once thresholds stabilize.
Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-5123/throughput-fingerprinting-canary-gates; dashboard prototype: https://grafana.internal.redwood/c/throughput-fingerprint.
